newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in to limit won's fall vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in to limit won's fall vs dlr.

text.p: The central bank of Korea intervened in the interbank market in early morning trading on Friday to cap the won decline against the dollar, dealers said.
But the bank denied the action, as it routinely does.
The Bank of Korea came in soon after the won opened at 847.50, the lowest level since a market average system was introduced in March 1990, dealers said.
Demand for the dollar is rising in line with increasing import deals, they said.
Traders said the won was expected to drop further without the central bank's support, traders said.
The won is currently trading at 846.50.
